title: clean lists the wrong trees for removal: a newline in a name lists a tree outside the project, a trailing TAB lists the source directory beside it, and a crate built with --target-dir . lists its own source
body:
FOUND 2026-09-23 by critic-shell's third pass on cc's rework of 0131, and PRE-EXISTING: lib/cmd/clean at 0.1.7 does all of it. DESTRUCTIVE: a real run removes what its list names, on a y at the prompt, without one under `clean --force`, and through `fullcycle`, which always hands clean `--force` (lib/cmd/fullcycle:289). DRIVEN by cc on 2026-09-24 at 6c9fbc6 with `clean rust --dry-run` only, each case beside a control that differs only in the crafted name. Every dry run exited 0, and afterwards every seeded directory was still present.

THREE MECHANISMS IN ONE SCAN, lib/cmd/clean:
- _clean_roots reads find's output one path per line (:234-243), so a name holding a newline becomes two paths.
- _clean_scan prints `status<TAB>path` rows and _clean_run reads them with `IFS=$'\t' read -r status d` (:445). TAB is an IFS whitespace character, so a trailing TAB in a name is stripped: the tree classified and the tree listed are two different directories.
- _clean_roots takes the directory of every `.rustc_info.json` and `CACHEDIR.TAG` as a candidate (:237-241), and _clean_has_markers accepts either as build output (:311-312). `cargo build --target-dir .` writes both into the crate's own root, so the crate is classified as a build tree, and its parent's manifest makes it removable.

DRIVEN:

1. A NEWLINE LISTS A TREE OUTSIDE THE PROJECT. Outside the project, a victim `outside1/victim/` holding a Cargo.toml and a tagged target/. Inside it, a directory named `x<newline>` whose subtree spells the victim's absolute path down to `target`. find prints one path, the read makes it two, and the second is the victim's real target/: "rust: 1 target tree(s)", naming `.../outside1/victim/target`, rc 0. THE CONTROL, the same subtree under a directory named `x`: its inner target/ is "ignored" (no markers), and "no removable target/ trees".

2. A TRAILING TAB LISTS THE SOURCE DIRECTORY. The project holds source `out/src/keep.rs` and a tagged build directory named `out<TAB>`. The scan classifies `out<TAB>` as removable, the read strips the TAB, and the list names `out`, the source directory. THE CONTROL, the build directory named `outx`: the list names `outx` and out/ is not listed.

3. A CRATE BUILT WITH `--target-dir .` LISTS ITS OWN SOURCE. A workspace member `member/` (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs) holding `.rustc_info.json` in its root: the list names `member`, since the workspace's Cargo.toml sits beside it. THE CONTROL, the same member without the file: "no removable target/ trees".

4. THE SAME AT THE PROJECT ROOT HIDES EVERY REAL TREE. `.rustc_info.json` at the project root beside a real tagged target/: the project root becomes the one candidate, is "skipped (no sibling Cargo.toml)", and every tree beneath it is dropped as nested (_clean_drop_nested, :253-264). The run ends "no removable target/ trees", rc 0, over a target/ it never listed. THE CONTROL, without the root file: target/ is listed.

In cases 2 and 3 the listed source directory's `src/` is also reported as another session's per-node cache under "THIS TREE IS SHARED", which is 0131's point 5. In case 4 the dry run wrote `.metadata_never_index` into the project root, which is 0131's point 4; a real run writes it there as well.

READ, NOT DRIVEN: a newline split that yields an existing directory INSIDE the project lists that directory the same way, and a yielded line that sorts before a real tree can make _clean_drop_nested drop the real tree from the scan as nested.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO:
- Carry every path whole from find to the removal: NUL-delimited reads, and no row joined on a character a name can hold between the scan and the run.
- List nothing outside PROJECT_ROOT. Every candidate is checked by its physical path to lie strictly beneath PROJECT_ROOT before it is classified, and one that does not is reported and never listed, so the guarantee does not rest on parsing alone.
- A directory that holds its own manifest is never a build tree, whatever markers it carries: it is reported as built in place, it is not removed or marked, and the trees beneath it are still scanned. PROJECT_ROOT is never a candidate.
- Arms: each of the four cases beside its control, red first at 6c9fbc6, with mutants.
- Pages: clean.md, where it says what a candidate is and what is skipped.

It is built inside 0131's rework of the same scan and closes with 0131 on one landing, as agreed with vc on 2026-09-24. cc's. It ships in 0.1.8 under hv's ruling.

## Resolution

Fixed at 81a8274, in 0131's commit, the rework of the same scan. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. find's output is NUL-delimited and read with `read -d ''`, its status taken by `wait` on the process substitution that carries it, and the scan's result lives in arrays from the walk to the removal, never joined into text: a newline or a TAB in a name no longer splits or strips it. A candidate not strictly beneath the project root stops the run as a devbin defect before anything is acted on, so the guarantee does not rest on parsing alone. A candidate holding its own manifest, and the project root itself, is set aside as built in place before the nesting test: it is never removed or marked, and the trees beneath it are still found. Every path the option prints itself is shell-quoted when it holds any byte that is not printable ASCII, read in the C locale, U+202E and an e-acute included, the root in the outside-root stop and in the partial note among them. The PATH guard gives a tree whose name ends in a newline its own check, its answer set through a nameref and read past a sentinel. clean.md says each of these.
- RED FIRST. The five first arms were red at ecd1149, on the four shapes the body drives and on a candidate outside the root reached through a stubbed find; there the old code removed the victim outside the project, the source out/ and the member crate's sources, inside the test sandbox. Each later arm was red on the tree its pass reviewed.
- MUTANTS. This issue's are each killed by the arm aimed at it: a line-at-a-time read, a stripped TAB, the outside candidate kept, a manifest-holding crate or the project root a candidate, a local shadowing the caller's array, a raw control character, only a control character quoting a name, pwd -P read through a stripping substitution, the display rule reading the caller's locale, and the outside-root stop printing the root raw.
- THE SUITE. As 0131's resolution.
